summary: Thomas Grahame Bailey worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. from the University of Edinburgh by 1920 and served as Reader in Hindustani at SOAS University of London from circa 1920 to 1940.

Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, Charing Cross Hospital and its Medical School, Imperial College School of Medicine, and University College London. He held a post at Imperial College London from circa 1854 to 1885.

Thomas Henry Thornton studied history, archaeology, and Indology at Merchant Taylors' School, St John's College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford. His career included posts at the East India Company, St John's College, University of Calcutta, and University of the Punjab.

Thomas Holbein Hendley studied at St Bartholomew's Hospital from circa 1864 to 1869. Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he held appointments with the Indian Medical Service starting in 1869 and as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta (1898-1903).

Thomas Howley, an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Bishop Cowie's Grammar School, served as Head-Master of the Anglo-Vernacular School. He became Professor of Tamil, Telugu and Hindustani at King's College London in 1861 and taught Telugu at Oxford (1878-1885).

Linguist Thomas Hudson-Williams studied at Ysgol Friars, Bangor University, University of London, and University of Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer. He spent his career at Bangor University as an Assistant Lecturer in French, German, and Classics, and later Professor of Greek (1904-1940).

Thomas James Mazanec, a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from Calvin University, CU Boulder, and Princeton University under multiple supervisors. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, where he became Associate Professor, and served as East Asia Section Editor for the AOS.

Thomas Jülch, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, Heidelberg University, University of Hull, and University of Munich (PhD). From 2013 to 2019, he was a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University.
Thomas Kintaert specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments at the University of Vienna, attested in 2009 and serving as a Lecturer attested between 2022 and 2026.
Thomas Lumisden Strange was an Indology scholar who completed his studies at Westminster School and the East India Company College between 1824 and 1826.
Thomas M. Hunter works in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He served as Dean at the University of Virginia and was affiliated with the University of British Columbia in 2011.

Thomas Manning worked in the fields of Tibetology and Sinology. He studied as a Scholar at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1790 to 1795 and later studied at Westminster Hospital from circa 1799 to 1800.

Thomas Maurice, an Indology and history/archaeology scholar, completed his B.A. and M.A. at the University of Oxford, studying at St John's and University College. He served as Assistant-Keeper of Manuscripts at the British Museum from 1798 to 1824.

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Cornell University under teacher Anne M. Blackburn. He held a post at the City University of Hong Kong attested in 2018.

Thomas Oberlies, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held posts at the universities of Tübingen, Zurich, and Freiburg, and served as Arbeitsstellenleiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Thomas Oldham studied at Trinity College Dublin and the University of Edinburgh. Working in history and archaeology, he served as Director of the Geological Survey of Ireland, Professor at Trinity College Hartford, Superintendent of the Geological Survey of India, and President of The Asiatic Society.

Thomas Procter was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. from Jesus College, Oxford, between 1818 and 1824. He later served as a Fellow at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1824-1826) and as an Examiner at Fort William College in 1828.

Thomas R. Trautmann, a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology, studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the University of Michigan, including serving as co-director attested in 1980 and with continued affiliation attested in 1991.

Thomas Robert Malthus was an English scholar who completed his education at Warrington Academy between circa 1782 and 1784, followed by studies at Jesus College, Cambridge, and the University of Cambridge from 1784 to circa 1788.

Thomas Robinson studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, receiving his B.A., M.A., and D.D. between 1808 and 1816. Specializing in linguistics, he held the post of Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from 1837 to 1854.
